name: Kochu Bata
subtitle: colocasia mashed with mustard and green chilli, eaten first with rice

ingredients.note: wear gloves peeling it; the raw sap irritates

ingredients.qty: 2 tbsp, soaked and ground to a paste

ingredients.note: raw, stirred in at the end, which is the Bengali way with a bata

prepNotes: A bata is a mash, eaten at the start of the meal with plain rice and a little raw mustard oil.
Colocasia must be cooked through completely. Undercooked it scratches the throat.

steps.text: Boil the colocasia in salted water with the turmeric until completely soft, about 20 minutes. Drain thoroughly.
steps.tip: Thoroughly. Any water left makes a sloppy bata.

steps.text: Mash it smooth while hot, or pulse briefly in a blender.
Grind the soaked mustard seeds with three of the green chillies and a pinch of salt into a paste.
Beat the mustard paste through the mash with the raw mustard oil and salt.
Temper the nigella and remaining chillies in a spoonful of hot oil and stir through.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. The mustard sharpens as it stands. Serve at room temperature, never hot.
